notes: A day of testing from five angles, and everything it turned up. A corrupt .ibt could take the whole machine down: opening about 5 KB of random bytes allocated until memory ran out - 42 GB and still climbing when it was killed - because the iRacing reader builds one object per buffer from a count it reads straight out of the file. A session truncated by a sim crash looks exactly like that. The header is now checked against the real file size before the reader opens it; all 188 real sessions here still load and a session iRacing is still writing is still accepted. Update installed the wrong version: a release downloaded in the morning sat ready while newer ones shipped, and pressing Update installed the stale file - it now rechecks and fetches the current one. Compare crashed on the first and last lap of any session against a reference, because those laps are partial and a missing value was divided. The corner tree crashed on a tight-apex corner with no throttle difference. The session cache never freed memory, reaching 3.9 GB after 160 sessions; it now keeps six. The bundled manual was missing six files including the Ask GOAT widget stylesheet and script, so the help widget inside it never worked. Escape now closes Debriefs, Highlights, Backup, Help, Dashboard, Feedback and Request, which all ignored the key. And --dir now means that folder: it was only applied to iRacing files, so an empty folder still listed 34 sessions from elsewhere. Checked and found sound: ten invariants over every saved reference, seven over 188 sessions, the career database, path traversal, malformed API input, and the delta-t trace, which agrees with real lap-time differences to 16 thousandths of a second at the median.
